pr.title: Don't build by-move body when async closure is tainted
pr.description:
Fixes #129676 

See explanation in the ui test.
pr.author: compiler-errors

processing.reason: The historical defect is not a value-level miscompilation that can be modeled by two same-signature Rust functions whose defined executions return different values. PR #129677 fixes a compiler error-recovery path in `rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine/by_move_body.rs`: before the fix, a tainted async-closure body still enters the lazy by-move-body builder, where `body.local_decls[ty::CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL].ty` is an error-folded type rather than `ty::Coroutine`, reaching `bug!`/ICE. After the fix, `if body.tainted_by_errors.is_some() { return coroutine_def_id.to_def_id(); }` skips construction and lets the original E0425 diagnostic be emitted. The added UI test `tests/ui/async-await/async-closures/tainted-body-2.rs` only asserts stderr; it does not execute a transformed program or observe any runtime value. Encoding the pre-fix behavior would require either an unconditional compiler panic or an arbitrary sentinel/return-value change to force a differential result. A panic is not a successful Miri execution, and a sentinel would not be the actual historical transformation. Therefore no source-grounded counterexample pair can satisfy the required value-difference harness without fabricating semantics.

evidence: Don't build by-move body when async closure is tainted
bug!("tried to create by-move body of non-coroutine receiver")
Ensure that building a by-ref async closure body doesn't ICE
We don't do numerical inference fallback when the body is tainted.
error[E0425]: cannot find value `missing` in this scope
error: aborting due to 1 previous error
analysis.incorrectTransformation: When typeck results are tainted by an earlier error, it still attempts to build the async closure's by-move body from the `mir_built` capture local. In the tainted case numerical inference fallback is skipped, so writeback can fold the coroutine-closure type (whose signature contains the numerical infer var) into an error type. The built/reference body's capture local is then not the expected `ty::Coroutine`, so the unconditional construction reaches a `bug!`/ICE instead of merely reporting the original diagnostic.
analysis.inputDomain: Edition 2021 programs using `#![feature(async_closure)]` with an async closure whose signature involves an inference variable and whose enclosing body has already been tainted by a type error. The regression input is a `main` containing the unresolved value `missing;` followed by `let c = async |_| {}; c(1);`, so writeback folds the coroutine-closure type into an error type because the closure parameter `_` is inferred from the later call.
analysis.originalLogic: `coroutine_by_move_body_def_id` unconditionally inspects `tcx.mir_built(coroutine_def_id)` and, after confirming the coroutine is a desugared closure, reads the capture-struct local type: "let coroutine_ty = body.local_decls[ty::CAPTURE_STRUCT_LOCAL].ty;" and then expects it to be a coroutine: "let ty::Coroutine(_, args) = *coroutine_ty.kind() else { bug!(\"{body:#?}\") };". It also later expects the parent to be a coroutine-closure and only checks for error references after that point: "if parent_args.references_error() { return coroutine_def_id.to_def_id(); }". There was no check of `body.tainted_by_errors` before building the by-move body.
pitfalls: Do not treat this as a general coroutine optimization change: it is error-recovery gating in the lazy by-move body builder.
Do not assume the existing `parent_args.references_error()` check is sufficient; the failure happens earlier when the capture-struct local does not match `ty::Coroutine`.
Skipping construction during tainted compilation is acceptable because the program is already erroneous; returning `coroutine_def_id.to_def_id()` is the recovery path.
Do not claim runtime reproduction or compiler execution from this historical patch; the evidence is a UI test expectation showing only E0425.
The new bug messages are diagnostic improvements for the same failure paths, not the functional fix.
preconditions: The by-move body is requested for a coroutine whose kind is a desugared closure (async closure).
The enclosing body already has a type error and its built MIR reports `tainted_by_errors`.
Numerical inference fallback is not performed for the tainted body, allowing writeback to fold the coroutine-closure type into an error type.
analysis.summary: StateTransform's lazy coroutine by-move body builder must skip construction when the source MIR is tainted by type errors; otherwise error-folded coroutine-closure types can reach a `bug!` assertion and ICE. The fix early-returns the original coroutine DefId before inspecting the capture struct.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI regression test (not an optimization-output test) in the async-closures area with `//@ edition: 2021` and `#![feature(async_closure)]`. Force a prior unresolved-name error (`missing;`) and an async closure with an inferred parameter (`let c = async |_| {}; c(1);`) so the tainted coroutine-closure signature is folded to an error type. Assert the only stderr is the original E0425 diagnostic and that no ICE occurs. To construct the minimal pair for a differential harness, keep the erroneous program identical and toggle only whether the tainted-body early return occurs before by-move body construction; the expected difference is an ICE versus a clean E0425, not a MIR value change.
analysis.trigger: The source body is marked tainted by errors (`body.tainted_by_errors.is_some()`) and the compiler requests the lazy by-move body for an async coroutine-closure, while the tainted writeback has produced a non-coroutine/error capture type.
